newsitem.title: DENMARK: Tele Danmark fights rivals with discounts.
newsitem.headline: Tele Danmark fights rivals with discounts.

text.p: Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark said on Friday it planned to introduce up to 20 percent discounts for business customers on overseas telephony to compete with new rivals on the recently-liberalised Danish telecoms market.

"We are considering discounts on overseas telephone calls of around 20 percent for business customers, with special individual discount deals for major clients," Tele Danmark Business Unit managing director Soeren Jensen told Reuters.
"We have made discount deals so far with 10-15 key clients. We are keeping a close eye on the competition so we can offer customers discounts at the same level as our rivals," he said.
Tele Danmark is offering major business clients bonus deals and discounts initially on overseas calls, possibly later on domestic calls, Jensen said.
Tele Danmark was partially privatised in 1994 with the Danish state holding on to a 51 percent stake. Denmark's telecoms sector was liberalised on July 1, 1996.
